statement.text: Four upper bounds. S1: speed v <= mu/(rho*D), i.e. Reynolds number <= 1 in water (no free constant). S2: unfed lifespan <= T_max, with T_max = 2 x the longest lifespan in development papers = 24 days. S3: radius R <= sqrt(6*Dox*C0/Q) = 0.548 mm (diameter 1.10 mm) for a sphere with uniform oxygen uptake (Dox 2e-9 m2/s, C0 0.25 mol/m3, Q 1e-2 mol/m3/s; no free constant). S4: replication generations G <= G_max = 2 x development maximum = 8. No checked Lean file under tracks/research/lean states any of these (CHECKED.txt has none on Reynolds, oxygen or replication). performance.verdict_basis: The lifetime bound held in 0 of 4 measurements: the held-out bots are fed, so the closed-energy-store assumption is false. The scorer also did not react to scrambled labels.

broken_input_control.description: quantity labels rotated by two places: coverage stayed 0.50, it did not get worse

items.what: 1) The energy-store lifetime law failed out of sample: 0 of 4 held-out lifespans are under the 24-day bound. Cause: the bound assumes a closed store (frog cells living on yolk); the held-out bots are human airway cells kept in culture medium with regular media changes, so the law's hypothesis is false for them.
